channel.title: Runway Briefing
channel.description: Your daily five-minute briefing on the aviation industry — new routes, airline strategy, fleet orders, and the moves shaping how we fly. Delivered daily like a friend catching you up over coffee.
channel.itunes:author: Runway Briefing

item.title: American's Widebody Gamble, Boeing's Air Force One Cracks, and Ukraine Warns the Skies Over Russia Are Closing
item.description: American Airlines is dangling up to 65 widebody jets in front of Airbus after years of retiring planes it probably shouldn't have. Boeing's Air Force One replacement is now getting patched for cracks on top of a $3 billion overrun, and Zelensky just told every airline still flying over Russia that the sky is about to get a lot less friendly. Plus, Emirates finally makes premium economy look like a real cabin instead of an afterthought.

item.title: Air Canada Goes Big, Southwest Gets Lounges, and a Cuba Flight Turns Into a Bomb Joke Nobody Should've Made
item.description: Air Canada just announced its biggest international expansion ever, and Southwest — the airline that used to brag about not having assigned seats — is building actual airport lounges with Chase. Plus, Zelensky tells airlines to stay out of Russian airspace entirely, Delta has a scary pattern with sick pilots, and one passenger in Miami picks the worst possible joke to make at a gate agent.

item.title: American Kills First Class, BA Guts Heathrow, and JetBlue Finally Gets a First Class Cabin
item.description: American Airlines unveils its swanky new Flagship Suites and sets a hard end date for international first class — while somehow also housing delayed passengers in a hotel with the ceiling ripped open. Plus, British Airways slashes 77 routes from Heathrow, JetBlue finally reveals its long-awaited domestic first class, and United's top status tier proves that loyalty, apparently, has a price tag of five million dollars.

item.title: Runway Briefing: United's Stranded Seats, Delta's Hawaii Whiplash, and JetBlue Buys Its Way Into LaGuardia
item.description: United bought hundreds of fancy lie-flat seats for a plane that still doesn't exist, and now they might not even fit. Delta can't decide if it wants to fly to Hawaii or not. Plus, JetBlue pays nearly sixty million bucks for old Spirit slots, and United's new app feature quietly makes life miserable for airline employees flying standby.

item.title: An Independent Reporter Loses His Home, Etihad Bets Big, and United's CEO Wants Chicago All to Himself
item.description: The founder of Aviation Herald, one of the most trusted names in aviation safety reporting, just lost his home fighting a defamation lawsuit for reporting something that turned out to be true. Plus, a Russian smuggling ring gets caught funneling spare parts to sanctioned Aeroflot, Etihad announces a massive $20 billion expansion plan, and United's Scott Kirby has some very convenient thoughts about American's struggles in Chicago.

item.title: Icahn Bails on JetBlue, Everyone's Cutting Routes, and Your Engine Oil Might Be Lying to You
item.description: Carl Icahn dumps his entire JetBlue stake at a loss after his board seats went up in smoke — so was this activist investing or just a really expensive shrug? Plus, Allegiant, Alaska, Frontier, and WestJet all take a hatchet to their fall schedules on the same day, a flight attendant union sounds the alarm on engine oil designed to NOT smell bad, and a Delta flight strands its own passengers after a TSA checkpoint closes for the night.

item.title: Episode Title: Air Canada's A321XLR Face-Plants on London, Delta and United Want to Be Singapore Airlines, and Frontier Guts Elite Status
item.description: Air Canada's shiny new A321XLR couldn't even make it through its debut season on the Toronto-London route before getting yanked. Plus, Delta's Ed Bastian and United's Scott Kirby are both suddenly dropping Singapore Airlines and Emirates in interviews, Qantas is retiring the A380 early, and Frontier's elite program gets stripped for parts. Grab a beer, this one's got some good absurdity in it.

item.title: Runway Briefing — United's Rough Day, Kirby's Chicago Prediction, and Frontier Plays Both Sides
item.description: A United flight from LA to Newark turns into a two-stop odyssey after an engine issue forces a diversion to Vegas. United's CEO doubles down on his prediction that American will eventually bail on Chicago. Frontier makes Diamond status easier to reach while quietly gutting everyone else's perks. Plus, Boeing's engineers just said "no thanks" to the latest contract, and two air traffic controllers are getting fired over the LaGuardia crash.
